A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UGround and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained method, experiments, and relocated supplementary material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original UGround benchmark results, component ablations, and layer-wise analyses, including Tables 3–8 and the appendix heatmaps.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds gating comparisons, resource measurements, MUSE and false-premise results, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The SSC/MasP procedure, Algorithm 1, and training objectives remain unchanged. However, v2 Table 13 marks UGround as operating without SAM, conflicting with the SAM-based architecture described throughout the paper. The PDFs do not establish whether this indicates an undocumented MUSE-specific adaptation or a table error.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on MUSE for multi-target reasoning segmentation and augmented FP-RefCOCO, FP-RefCOCO+, and FP-RefCOCOg for false-premise recognition and segmentation (Tables 13–14). These extend the tested task requirements beyond v1's ReasonSeg, RefCOCO variants, and gRefCOCO, despite v1 already claiming these broader capabilities.

E2.justification: Table 4 removes POPEN-7B and adds CoRes. v2 also introduces a non-RL soft-gating comparator in Table 10, LISA-rec and LISA-aug variants in Table 13, and Cascading in Table 14. These changes add substantive alternatives for assessing layer selection and broader grounding capabilities; most existing comparator rows remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds a dedicated resource-evaluation protocol: an A100-SXM4-40GB GPU, 400 training samples over 200 steps with batch size 2, and inference over 799 test samples with batch size 1. It introduces latency, peak memory, parameter, and FPS measurements, plus separate 'see' and segmentation evaluation for false-premise queries. The previously stated ReasonSeg training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining Tables 6–8 and the original layer heatmaps, v2 adds an RL-versus-soft-gating analysis, comparative computational-cost measurements, and extensive qualitative case studies on reasoning, multiple targets, and false-premise rejection (Figures 7–11). These provide new evidence about component choice, practical costs, and model behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The Monte Carlo dropout analogy already appears in v1; its expansion in v2 does not introduce measured predictive uncertainty or a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Common entries in Tables 2–8 retain their numerical scores, while Table 4 adds CoRes results and removes POPEN results. New Tables 10–14 substantially expand the findings, including MUSE cIoU of 56.4 on validation and 50.4 on test, false-premise scores, and UGround measurements of 2.97 seconds per training iteration and 4.12 FPS. These are newly reported results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 now explicitly defines the ground-truth mask on a discrete pixel grid and specifies a piecewise-constant extension to the continuous plane before Gaussian convolution. v1 simply treats the mask as a continuous-plane function. This is a limited formal refinement; the principal equations and policy-gradient formulation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same attribute-based unification claim, SSC/MasP contribution, and headline gains of 9.0% cIoU and 12.1% N-acc. The additional experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds substantive arguments about discrete layer selection, soft-gating feature dilution, objective alignment, and prompting costs. Appendix G replaces v1's brief future-work direction with specific limitations: fragmented, displaced, incomplete, or collapsed masks, attributed to imperfect geometric alignment despite correct semantic grounding, and uncertainty about SAM's decoding behavior.

D1.justification: v2 documents eight dataset categories and their constituent datasets, describes mixed training as needed, and supplies similarity-map dimensions and SAM prompt-encoder shapes in Appendix C and Table 15. It also specifies resource-measurement hardware and procedures. These substantially expand implementation disclosure, although exact training mixtures are not mapped to individual results. Code and model access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to CoRes, Gal and Ghahramani's dropout work, CLIP, and Zhang et al.'s layer-relevance work, while removing POPEN. These support added comparisons and explanations. The main related-work taxonomy and positioning around attribute-oriented unification remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the single supplementary-statements appendix into thematic Appendices A–G, separating retained implementation, visualization, and disclosure material. It adds a notation guide and substantial worked explanations of gating and prompting, and rewrites parts of Sections 3.2, 4.1, and the RefCOCO discussion. The main section sequence and much introductory language remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, with resized and reformatted displays and clearer Figure 2 axis labels. v2 adds Tables 9–15 and qualitative Figures 7–11. The original heatmaps are retained as Figures 4–6; the repository diagram moves to Figure 13, and the dashboard becomes Figure 12 with an additional example.

improvement.justification: The new gating comparison, specified resource measurements, and concrete failure limitations make the unchanged method better supported and easier to assess. However, comparison quality is weakened by removing POPEN, which exceeded UGround on RefCOCOg validation in v1 (75.4 versus 74.7), and by Table 13's unresolved contradiction about SAM usage. These tradeoffs support a limited net improvement rather than an unqualified substantial gain.
